questions.question: You should ___ click on a link sent to you by a stranger.
questions.explanation: Never click on links from people you don't recognize, no matter how legitimate they may seem.

questions.question: If you see a popup that tells you you've won something for free, what should you do?
choices: Click on it and get your free stuff
Click on it to see if it's real
questions.explanation: Free giveaways and raffles online are almost always scams. Any popup advertising that you've won something you don't recognize should be avoided.

questions.question: If you get a popup telling you 'your device is infected with malware, click here', what should you do?
choices: Send it to your friend to see what they think
Click on it and follow the instructions
Ignore the popup and close the website
questions.explanation: Popups encouraging you to click them should always be treated as suspicious, even if they seem helpful. Never trust something encouraging you to click or download something you don't recognize.

questions.question: If you get a text message from a number you don't know telling you your device has been hacked, what should you do?
choices: Tell a trusted adult and don't follow any instructions
Ignore it and don't tell anyone
questions.explanation: Scammers often try to make you panic by telling you you're in trouble and need to follow their instructions without thinking. Always talk to a trusted adult before doing anything.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT do before clicking a website link?
choices: Check if the link is spelled correctly
Make your friend click it first to see what happens
Make sure you recognize where the link is taking you and who sent it
Don't click it if it seems suspicious
questions.explanation: Links can be helpful when navigating the web, but make sure you know who sent it and where it's taking you. Some websites try to trick people by using links spelled slightly differently from real sites.

questions.question: If a game asks you for ___ before you can play, it's ok to give it to them.
questions.explanation: Don't trust any games or sites that ask you for information they don't need. No game online needs personal information to work.

questions.question: If you get an unusual message from a friend online telling you to click a link, you should NOT ___.
choices: Trust your friend and click it
Contact them through some other method and ask about it
Tell people you know to be wary that this person may have been hacked
Block their account until you get more information
questions.explanation: If someone you know sends you a strange message, their account may have been stolen. Let them know and warn others who might receive messages from that account.

questions.question: Scammers often try to ___ so you follow their instructions.
questions.explanation: Scammers often try to make you panic by telling you something scary so you follow instructions without thinking. Stay calm and ask a trusted adult if you're unsure what to do.

questions.question: What's one way to tell if a website is legitimate?
choices: If the URL starts with https://
If the URL starts with http://
If the site popped up when you searched something
questions.explanation: A website starting with https:// has encryption enabled, which often indicates it is more secure. However, you should still be cautious because not all sites online are trustworthy.

questions.question: Never give ___ to a website you don't trust.
questions.explanation: Unless you know the website you're using is safe, don't give it personal information. It's important to protect your privacy at all times.

questions.question: If a website asks to use your camera when it doesn't seem like it should need it, you should ___.
choices: Allow it to use your camera
Deny the permissions and close the website
Point your camera at the floor so it can't see you
questions.explanation: A website should only ask to use your camera if there is a clear reason, never give permissions to websites just because they ask.

questions.question: Website URL's starting with https:// are ___.
questions.explanation: A website starting with https:// has encryption enabled, which usually means it's trustworthy. Plenty of websites will try to look official, but not everything you find online is safe.

questions.question: Scammers frequently use ___ to try and get you to follow their instructions
questions.explanation: Scammers will often try to make you panic by telling you you're in trouble and need to follow their instructions without thinking. Stay calm when strangers tell you something scary, and tell an adult if you're not sure what to do.

questions.question: If a phone number you don't recognize calls you and says you were accepted into something you didn't apply for, that is almost certainly a ___.
questions.explanation: If you didn't apply for something, there's no reason you should be accepted into it. Scammers will often impersonate rewards programs or offer special deals/benefits to trick you.

questions.question: A website ending in ___. is probably safe.
questions.explanation: .org is a trusted domain used by professional organization to prove they are trustworthy, typically a website ending in .org is safe.

questions.question: If a person you don't know asks to call or message you, there's a good chance they are ___.
questions.explanation: It's a safe practice to be wary of strangers reaching out to you, especially if they want to convince you to call them or have a conversation.

questions.question: If someone calls you claiming to be your bank and asks you to transfer or deposit money to a different account, what should you do?
choices: Hang up and block the number
Ask them to prove they're really your bank
questions.explanation: Your bank may call you for a number of reasons, but they will never ask you to give them a password or transfer money into a different account.

questions.question: If someone sends you a link to download a movie or game for free, you should ___.
choices: Send it to a friend to see what happens
Ask them to prove it's real
questions.explanation: NEVER click on links from people you don't recognize, no matter how legitimate they may seem.

questions.question: If you accidentally click a suspicous link, what should you do?
choices: Close it and tell a trusted adult or run an antivirus scan
questions.explanation: Clicking a supicious link might happen, but the important thing to do when it does is to make sure you take steps to stop anything worse from happening.

questions.question: If a website asks you for a password to a different app or site, you should be ___.
questions.explanation: Websites shouldn't ask you for a password for an account used on another platform without a very clear reason. Be cautious giving up your password anywhere.

questions.question: In general, you should ___ clicking on random pop ups
questions.explanation: It's a good practice to avoid clicking on pop ups in general. Even if they're just ads, you have no reason to pay attention to them.

questions.question: If your friend sends you a link and tells you to click on it with no explanation, you should ___.
choices: Contact them through some other method and ask about it
Tell some other friend to click it first
questions.explanation: If someone you know sends you a strange message, it's possible their account has been stolen. Make sure you let them and anyone who might be contacted by their account know right away and don't reply.

questions.question: Websites that look official are ___ legitimate.
questions.explanation: Plenty of websites look pretty and professional, but that doesn't make them trustworthy. Don't let presentation stand as proof that a website is safe.

questions.question: If a person contacts you online claiming to be ___, it is safe to trust them.
choices: Tech support looking to fix a problem
An employer offering a job you don't recognize
questions.explanation: Scammers will impersonate anyone they think you might respond to. If someone strange reaches out to you unexpectedly, you should always be skeptical.

questions.question: Stealing someones personal informtion to impersonate (pretend to be) them is called what?
questions.explanation: Identity theft is when someone steals your personal information to pretend to be you online, buying things under your name, accessing personal accounts, and other harmful things.
